UP IN FLAMES

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A frightening trend hits affluent suburbs in Johannesburg – homes are broken into and set alight.

Unique Selling Point:
** TOPICAL CURRENTLY
** SOME CCTV footage
** CELLPHONE FOOTAGE OF HOMES UP IN FLAMES

Summary:
Criminals break into homes, sometimes they steal valuables, sometimes they don’t - but what they do is set the homes alight as a parting gift.

The homeowners are up in arms, other media have latched onto it and are running with a sensationalist – it’s a lone arsonist - angle – but we unpack the facts and test the theories – exploring the modus operandis and the motives.


Further information:
THE NUMBERS SO FAR
I’ve spoken to 11 home owners personally, but have confirmed 12 in total through other journo and fire investigator. (possibly one more bringing it to 13)

One in Feb 2020 – 11 in a space of 11 months (first one in May 2021)- I’ve made a spreadsheet of the details.

FOOTAGE
I have footage of some of the houses going up in flames, I also have some CCTV footage of the suspect and some of emergency teams arriving at one of the scenes.

WHAT THE HOMEOWNERS ARE SAYING
IT’s AN ARSONIST. But is it?

WHAT THE EXPERTS ARE SAYING
Impossible to pin it on one person – the MO’s are different. While there are elements that are the same in some cases – there are others that vary.

WHAT WE KNOW
1. Are the homes occupied? YES & NO.
2. Is there interaction with the people in the house? YES & NO – sometimes the people are assaulted – sometimes not. The most recent case saw the old man assaulted and then locked in the house while it was set alight?
3. Was the alarm triggered? YES & NO. In two instances ADT & CAP Security responded but failed to go inside when the suspect/s were in side.
4. What does the CCTV footage show? In two of the cases it shows a lone man on the property – some footage of the guy inside the one house and in the other case he is seen trying to break in? In two of the cases the cameras were cut.
5. What is stolen? Very difficult to tell because in many of the cases everything is burnt to the ground. But where there has been instances where things are stolen – it’s a laptop, a cellphone or a handbag.

THE CASE STUDIES
Most of these people are reluctant to talk, some fear retaliation, some worry about insurance claims and other about property values. Andre Snyman will paint the picture of the extent – he has been to many of the scenes and spoken to many of the victims – we’ll go on a ride-along with him to some of the scenes and film it in an immersive in situ style.

ON-SCREEN CASE STUDY
Of the 11 I spoke to only one was willing to do the interview – but they are living in the Western Cape and commute. The other option is the most recent victim – working on them still. There story is great!

BACKGROUND TO MOST RECENT VICTIM
We’ll interview the son – he wasn’t home but is animated and tells the story well according to Gill Gifford from The Times.

The father, an elderly man was home alone, there was a knock on the door – he went to open and got assaulted. Some items were stolen, it is believed to have been a single black male – he then locked the old man in the house and set alight.

The neighbours found a bottle of wine and a bag of apples in their garden. The son confirms it was from their house. The theory is that the suspect watched the home burn as he ate the apples and drank the wine. This feeds into the theory of a possible arsonist.

** HOPEFULLY he’ll confirm with me over the weekend. Alternately we have to do the lady that lives in Franschoek. She also feels it’s an arsonist – has CCTV footage that she has shared.

KEY MOTIVES
1. A PYROMANIAC – someone who just wants to watch it BURN – they will usually stay in the area and watch the fire as a bystander afterwards. Often CCTV cameras in the neighbourhood will pick up the same suspect at the scenes.
2. EVIDENCE DESTRUCTION – thieves that want to destroy an evidence / finger prints that could link them to the scene.
3. REVENGE – fuelled by disgruntled employees / upset love relationships.
4. SELF-STARTERS – homeowners could cause fires for false insurance claims.
5. AND WAIT FOR IT…. LOADSHEDDING – some fires could be as a result of electrical faults triggered by power surges linked to loadshedding.

UNDERSTANDING THE PSYCHE OF A FIRESTARTER
Anni Hesselink is a Criminologist – she has been interviewed on arson previously when there was the Cape Town fires. She will speak to the personality trends and motives.

KEY ELEMENTS TO COVER
- PROPERTY VALUES: Many of the case studies are so nervous about being interviewed because they don’t want to affect their property prices.
- INSURANCE: The homeowners are put through a lot with insurance – often taking months to settle these claims
- SECURITY: We have a false sense of security – often thinking we are safer than we actually are. A lot of the time there were possible red flags – alarm triggers dismissed as a false alarm, sometimes the alarm wasn’t armed, and sometimes the security companies didn’t actually respond properly
- FIRE SAFETY: Prioritising fire safety – what to do, what to have on hand.

FIRE INVESTIGATOR
We speak to Wynand Engelbrecht from a private fire fighting operation. They have been to at least 5 of the scenes. And have spoke to some of the other fire investigators and have compared notes. I feel he is the most equipped to comment. COJ apparently haven’t sent out fire investigators to all of the scenes.

We clarify how fires are started, how fast they spread and ask about accelerants, locations of the initial fires and talk about fire safety.

Tracey Pennington
Jacqui Fox HOUSE FIRE VICTIM
Kosta Babich HOUSE FIRE VICTIM

Expert:
Mr. Andre Snyman
Mr. Wynand Engelbrecht Retired Fire Chief FIRE OPS SA

Script:


STRUCTURE: FIRES

2 SECONDS MUSIC OVER DRONE SHOT BEFORE VO STARTS ON THE HOUSE

VO: The walls of this home in the leafy Johannesburg suburb of Dunkeld were once lined with contemporary South African art; the rooms filled with music. All that’s left are memories and the charred remnants of an unstoppable fire.

JOCELYN: It was the most terrible shock in our lives. // one shouldn't have to go through this

VO: Now, in a city already paranoid about security, anxiety is spreading in its northern suburbs.

LINK: // high walls, electric fences, armed response, fancy alarms. You think you've got it covered, right?

VO: BUT fire is unpredictable, menacing and devastating. Even more so if it’s arson.

TRACY: We definitely live with a false sense of security,//

VO: In just 12 months there’s been at least 11 suspicious house fires in a relatively concentrated area. Tracey Pennington’s modern Hurlingham home was hit in November last year when they were out of town - their safe space, burnt, to the ground.

TRACY: It's so destructive, setting it on fire. //And it's amazing that so many months later that I feel the way that I do. i just have my moments.//

VO: With nothing stolen from the property, Tracey is convinced the suspect was no amateur and his sole purpose was to burn down the house.

This is possibly the only CCTV Footage of a suspect - this shows a man attempting to break in on the night of the fire.

TRACY: we have no footage of him around the house. He cut the cameras and he would have to be on the roof. ////We know the siren went off on the first alarm activation, he cut it

VO: Anni Hesselink is a criminologist and criminal profiler.

ANNI: That tells me he can operate in terms of surveillance. Maybe he has a history in working with in the security field where he knows how to disable them and not to be detected.M11

VO: Once inside the Hurlingham house, the exclusive footage shows he acted alone - you can see him walking up and down the passage.

TRACY: // We can track him walking directly from the kitchen where he broken through the skylight straight into our main bedroom. And we know from investigations that he set three fires in the main bedroom, in the bathroom and in our dressing room. // it's just hard to fathom that somebody would do that to somebody else.

VO: In the world of criminal profiling, the suspect will fall into one of two categories.

ANNI: We distinguish between an arsonist. That is a criminal act, versus pyromania, which is a psycho psychiatric disorder - there is that enjoyment of the fire.

VO: But were the 11 suspicious house fires mere coincidence or the work of a lone fire starter?

We found similarities and clear discrepancies - of the 11, seven of the targeted properties were not occupied when the fires started. All of the structures are not architecturally the same - some had basic security while some had advanced systems.

ANDRE: I reckon that within a five kilometre radius, most of the houses were burnt.

VO: Since last year, Community Security Activist Andre Snyman has maintained the fires are connected.

ANDRE: I don't think that these are random houses / You can't just arrive here like a smash and grab. It's a well thought out, well-planned.

ANNI: I think there is a pattern of target selection, specifically one population or a class, a social class of people. //Where the modus operandi is not always the same, but the purpose of destruction and damage and the fire setting that the end result is always the same.

VO: Snyman took us to some of the more recent scenes.

ANDRE: The houses I've been to are massive fires. It doesn't look just like a little fire.

VO: This double storey Houghton Estate home was burnt down in April, just weeks earlier. The blaze ripped through the roof and shattered the windows, leaving only the soot covered walls and mere memories of the life once lived here.

LINK: // The trauma is still palpable and the family refuses to speak because they just don't know how they're going to pick up the pieces.

VO: The suspect locked the elderly homeowner inside, set the house alight, and left.

ANDRE: the old man was at the bottom shouting. He had been beaten up, but he was behind the burglar proofing they couldn't get him out

VO: Fortunately, security and neighbours managed to free the elderly man - he was in ICU weeks after the attack and is still recovering.

ANNI: //The moment this perpetrator walks into the house, he's got power and control over the house, over the occupants of the house
BONGANI: And it's not necessarily about even stealing anything from these homes.
ANNI: //It's about a fascination, an obsession, the immediate gratification of the hurt and the damage // It might be linked to hatred, to jealousy, with definitely an underlying mental disorder, psychological disorder, antisocial personality.

VO: Snyman believes the fire starter spends time in some of the homes and possibly even stays to watch the blaze.

ANDRE: Sometimes he eats, sometimes he drinks, sometimes he wees in the in the kitchen// At this particular house. He actually took apples and some wine and he sat in the neighbors property on that side and he ate the apples and he drank the wine. I think he did that while he was watching the fire from the neighbour's property and they identified those apples in the wine, because this old man apparently had bought those apples and wine.

VO: But the March Houghton Estate incident wasn’t the first time elderly homeowners were brutally assaulted. A Bryanston couple, still reeling from the attack in their home last December, agreed to an interview on condition of anonymity.

KOSTA: Well, we are terrified. // I sometimes dream about this incident AND SO DOES MY WIFE

VO: The couple were physically attacked by a single suspect who - ironically - sprayed them with a fire extinguisher.

After demanding jewellery and cash the couple didn’t have in the house, the attack took a sinister turn.

KOSTA: I SAW THAT HE HAD A FIRE-LIGHTER //He then went passed me saying, the fire will kill me and he must now go.

VO: The couple were left for dead, while flames engulfed their home.

Again this suspect was a lone fire starter, but it appears in this case the first intent was possibly theft.

Arson cases are not uncommon in SOuth Africa, with 3225 incidents reported between April and December 2021.

ANNI: this crime is on the rise in South Africa. And also it's most probably the prevalence is most probably that it's a male that is involved // in this type of crime. //

VO: But that’s not to say it involves the same male suspect.

LINK: It seems obvious these fires in most cases were started by someone. The question is why? It's even trickier when you think about the modus operandi.

ANNI: We are looking much wider than just a single person with the same modus operandi.
BONGANI: The pyromaniac doesn't explain necessarily all the fires.
ANNI: Not necessarily. It has a ripple effect on people taking advantage of the situation. // It might spur other individuals to commit arson for insurance purposes

VO: The motive could even have been a double criminal act; the thieves wanting to destroy evidence after a burglary.

The art and music-filled house in Dunkeld had been in Jocelyn Fox’s family since 1959.

JOCELYN: It was a Wonderful Life. Until these people came in and they burnt it down. Out of the blue.

VO: Her daughter Jacqui Fox says the family is still trying to make sense of it all.

BONGANI: The destruction was extreme. I mean, there's not much left of your home.
JACQUI: It's absolutely, absolutely traumatic because it's something it’s. it’s, you know, you can't replace these things.

VO: It’s a substantial financial loss and Jacqui suspects foul play.

JACQUI: I have a passion for contemporary South African art and all that. Has gone and left before fire without question.
BONGANI Do you think the motive was the theft of what's missing?
JACQUI: Yes, the motive was the art. This was a burglary.

VO: And if that is the case, this fire was an attempted cover up. But understanding the science of fire goes beyond just setting it. Former Fire Chief Wynand Engelbrecht attended six of the fires in question.

WYNAND: You can't possibly destroy all the evidence by creating a fire. there are always clues left.
VO: But with different insurance companies, a network of fire investigators and a number of security companies working in silos - the jury is out on whether it’s a definite trend.

WYNAND: Two or three swallows don't make the summer. I'm convinced there is no trend yet.

ANDRE: I don't know. Bongani, I'm as confused as everybody else.And this is a challenge amongst the security companies and the police to do the job.

VO: With so many unanswered questions and no clear suspects - homeowners are on edge. Incidents appear on the rise, with a suspicious fire having been reported in the area every two weeks since the beginning of March.

LINK: //As we were filming this story. This home was burnt down. The owners have barely recovered from the shock. The entire bottom section of this house has been completely burnt out.

VO: The suspect appears to have removed the front door key, essentially trapping the elderly couple sleeping upstairs. Luckily, they managed to escape through the garage, while flames engulfed their home.

BONGANI: It's actually quite traumatic, even when lives are not lost.
ANNI: You have to start all over again. And that is very devastating. // and the community live in fear because no one knows who's next. M18



STUDIO OUTTRO
Emboldended with no arrests

 
PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 11 SECONDS
VO: Affluent suburbs in Johannesburg appear to be targeted with nearly a dozen upmarket homes broken into and set alight – is the work of a lone fire starter or just coincidence?

PROMO 2 – 21 SECONDS
VO: Criminals break into affluent homes. Sometimes they steal valuables, sometimes they don’t - but one they are doing…. is setting the homes alight.

ANDRE: I reckon that within a five kilometre radius, most of the houses were burnt.

VO: Are these targeted attacks or mere coincidence?

PROMO 3 – 21 seconds
VO: Homeowners are on edge as fear mounts following a trail of devastating fires gutting properties in Joburg’s affluent northern suburbs.

ANNI: I think there is a pattern of target selection, specifically one population or a class, a social class of people.

VO: We put the pieces together looking at motives and modus operandi.

metadata.Summary: Criminals break into homes, sometimes they steal valuables, sometimes they don’t - but what they do is set the homes alight as a parting gift. The homeowners are up in arms, other media have latched onto it and are running with a sensationalist – it’s a lone arsonist - angle – but we unpack the facts and test the theories – exploring the modus operandis and the motives.
metadata.Further information: THE NUMBERS SO FAR I’ve spoken to 11 home owners personally, but have confirmed 12 in total through other journo and fire investigator. (possibly one more bringing it to 13) One in Feb 2020 – 11 in a space of 11 months (first one in May 2021)- I’ve made a spreadsheet of the details. FOOTAGE I have footage of some of the houses going up in flames, I also have some CCTV footage of the suspect and some of emergency teams arriving at one of the scenes. WHAT THE HOMEOWNERS ARE SAYING IT’s AN ARSONIST. But is it? WHAT THE EXPERTS ARE SAYING Impossible to pin it on one person – the MO’s are different. While there are elements that are the same in some cases – there are others that vary. WHAT WE KNOW 1. Are the homes occupied? YES & NO. 2. Is there interaction with the people in the house? YES & NO – sometimes the people are assaulted – sometimes not. The most recent case saw the old man assaulted and then locked in the house while it was set alight? 3. Was the alarm triggered? YES & NO. In two instances ADT & CAP Security responded but failed to go inside when the suspect/s were in side. 4. What does the CCTV footage show? In two of the cases it shows a lone man on the property – some footage of the guy inside the one house and in the other case he is seen trying to break in? In two of the cases the cameras were cut. 5. What is stolen? Very difficult to tell because in many of the cases everything is burnt to the ground. But where there has been instances where things are stolen – it’s a laptop, a cellphone or a handbag. THE CASE STUDIES Most of these people are reluctant to talk, some fear retaliation, some worry about insurance claims and other about property values. Andre Snyman will paint the picture of the extent – he has been to many of the scenes and spoken to many of the victims – we’ll go on a ride-along with him to some of the scenes and film it in an immersive in situ style. ON-SCREEN CASE STUDY Of the 11 I spoke to only one was willing to do the interview – but they are living in the Western Cape and commute. The other option is the most recent victim – working on them still. There story is great! BACKGROUND TO MOST RECENT VICTIM We’ll interview the son – he wasn’t home but is animated and tells the story well according to Gill Gifford from The Times. The father, an elderly man was home alone, there was a knock on the door – he went to open and got assaulted. Some items were stolen, it is believed to have been a single black male – he then locked the old man in the house and set alight. The neighbours found a bottle of wine and a bag of apples in their garden. The son confirms it was from their house. The theory is that the suspect watched the home burn as he ate the apples and drank the wine. This feeds into the theory of a possible arsonist. ** HOPEFULLY he’ll confirm with me over the weekend. Alternately we have to do the lady that lives in Franschoek. She also feels it’s an arsonist – has CCTV footage that she has shared. KEY MOTIVES 1. A PYROMANIAC – someone who just wants to watch it BURN – they will usually stay in the area and watch the fire as a bystander afterwards. Often CCTV cameras in the neighbourhood will pick up the same suspect at the scenes. 2. EVIDENCE DESTRUCTION – thieves that want to destroy an evidence / finger prints that could link them to the scene. 3. REVENGE – fuelled by disgruntled employees / upset love relationships. 4. SELF-STARTERS – homeowners could cause fires for false insurance claims. 5. AND WAIT FOR IT…. LOADSHEDDING – some fires could be as a result of electrical faults triggered by power surges linked to loadshedding. UNDERSTANDING THE PSYCHE OF A FIRESTARTER Anni Hesselink is a Criminologist – she has been interviewed on arson previously when there was the Cape Town fires. She will speak to the personality trends and motives. KEY ELEMENTS TO COVER - PROPERTY VALUES: Many of the case studies are so nervous about being interviewed because they don’t want to affect their property prices. - INSURANCE: The homeowners are put through a lot with insurance – often taking months to settle these claims - SECURITY: We have a false sense of security – often thinking we are safer than we actually are. A lot of the time there were possible red flags – alarm triggers dismissed as a false alarm, sometimes the alarm wasn’t armed, and sometimes the security companies didn’t actually respond properly - FIRE SAFETY: Prioritising fire safety – what to do, what to have on hand. FIRE INVESTIGATOR We speak to Wynand Engelbrecht from a private fire fighting operation. They have been to at least 5 of the scenes. And have spoke to some of the other fire investigators and have compared notes. I feel he is the most equipped to comment. COJ apparently haven’t sent out fire investigators to all of the scenes. We clarify how fires are started, how fast they spread and ask about accelerants, locations of the initial fires and talk about fire safety.
